items.title: R.C.H. Smith Interview, 1975-10-02
items.q: associated with the era of Bill Haley and the Comets and that kind of thing.

ctx.x: I mean, the crowd. There must have been a good-sized crowd.

Oh, a good-sized crowd. Yeah, lots of fans in those days. The so-called Dixieland was quite a big thing. This is pre-Elvis Presley. Pre-rock. In fact, I was living and working in New York when Alan Freed came out of, I think it was Cleveland, to break it up in New York and he came into town using the name Moondog, which had been his radio name in Cleveland. And then the real Moondog, the street musician, promptly sued him and won. So Alan Freed had to just become Alan Freed and then he went on to be rock promoter…
who was in the Ori band.
